description: Add cloud provider documentation support (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare) with new llms-index adapter, sitemap index support, GitHub adapter enhancements, topic prefixing, rate limiting, and CLI improvements for large libraries

userStories.title: Add cloud provider types to types.ts

Add optional maxFiles field (number) to GithubConfig for GitHub safety limit
Add optional subDirs field (string array) to GithubConfig for subdirectory scoping
Add optional topicPrefix field ('none' | 'directory' | 'auto') to SourceConfig, default 'none'

userStories.title: Create llms-index adapter with both content types
userStories.description: As a developer, I need an adapter that follows a root llms.txt index to per-service llms.txt or llms-full.txt files so that I can ingest cloud provider docs.
acceptanceCriteria: Create packages/scraper/src/adapters/llms-index.ts
Adapter fetches root URL and extracts per-service URLs using the servicePattern regex from config
include/exclude patterns filter discovered service URLs
maxServices config limits how many services are processed (default 1000)
For contentType 'llms-full': fetches each service URL, passes through cleanMarkdown and splitTopics, prefixes all topic IDs with service slug
For contentType 'llms-txt': fetches each service URL, parses as llms.txt (extracts .md links), fetches each linked page, cleans content, creates topics with service-prefixed IDs
Concurrent service processing in batches of 4 using Promise.allSettled
Individual service failures are logged and skipped (graceful degradation)
Services producing fewer than 2 topics are skipped with a warning
Console progress logging: 'Processing service X/Y: {serviceName}'
Topic titles include service context (e.g., 'Workers: Routing')
Register adapter in the adapter lookup (scrape.ts or wherever adapters are mapped)
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Core new adapter. Reuse fetchContent from pipeline/fetch.ts, cleanMarkdown from pipeline/clean.ts, splitTopics from pipeline/split.ts. See existing adapters (llms-full.ts, llms-txt.ts) for patterns. The adapter must also be registered in scrape.ts so the orchestrator can use it.

userStories.title: Enhance GitHub adapter with subDirs, maxFiles, and truncation fallback
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the GitHub adapter to handle very large repos like MicrosoftDocs/azure-docs (26.7GB) so that I can ingest Azure documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: When subDirs is set in GithubConfig, only process files within those subdirectories of docsPath (e.g., docsPath 'articles', subDirs ['azure-functions', 'cosmos-db'] → only files under articles/azure-functions/ and articles/cosmos-db/)
When subDirs is not set, existing behavior (all files under docsPath) is preserved
maxFiles config (default 10000) limits total number of files processed; log warning when limit reached
Detect truncated tree API response (truncated: true in JSON); when detected, log warning and fall back to per-directory GitHub Contents API calls for each subDir path
Contents API fallback: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch} for each subDir, filter for .md/.mdx files
Update packages/scraper/src/__tests__/adapters/github.test.ts with new tests
Test: subDirs filters to specified directories only
Test: without subDirs, all files under docsPath are included (backwards compat)
Test: maxFiles limits file count
Test: truncated tree triggers Contents API fallback
Test: Contents API fallback fetches per subDir
100% coverage maintained on github.ts
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: See packages/scraper/src/adapters/github.ts for existing implementation. The tree API endpoint is GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{branch}?recursive=1. Contents API is GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={branch}.

userStories.title: Add topic ID prefixing to GitHub adapter
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the GitHub adapter to prefix topic IDs with subdirectory names so that topics from different cloud services don't collide.
acceptanceCriteria: When topicPrefix is 'directory' or 'auto' in source config: prefix each topic ID with the immediate subdirectory name under docsPath (e.g., file at articles/azure-functions/overview.md → topic ID 'azure-functions-overview')
When topicPrefix is 'none' (default): existing behavior, no prefix (backwards compatible)
Topic titles also include the subdirectory as context (e.g., 'Azure Functions: Overview')
Subdirectory slug is derived by slugifying the directory name
Files directly under docsPath (no subdirectory) get no prefix regardless of setting
Update github.test.ts with tests for prefixing behavior
Test: directory prefix mode prefixes IDs correctly
Test: none mode has no prefix (backwards compat)
Test: files at docsPath root get no prefix
100% coverage maintained
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: The subdirectory is derived from the file path: for path 'articles/azure-functions/overview.md' with docsPath 'articles', the subdirectory is 'azure-functions'. Use slugify() from utils.ts for the prefix.

userStories.title: Integrate rate limiter into fetch pipeline
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the rate limiter wired into the scraper so that cloud provider scraping respects rate limits.
acceptanceCriteria: Modify scrape.ts: read rateLimit from source config, create a RateLimiter instance, pass it to adapter.process()
Extend Adapter.process() signature in types.ts to accept optional RateLimiter parameter
GitHub adapter: call rateLimiter.acquire() before each fetch call; also check X-RateLimit-Remaining header and pause if below 100
Sitemap adapter: call rateLimiter.acquire() before each page fetch
HTML adapter: call rateLimiter.acquire() before each page fetch
llms-index adapter: call rateLimiter.acquire() before each service/page fetch
llms-full and llms-txt adapters: minimal change — acquire once before main fetch (these only fetch 1-2 URLs)
Default rate limit is 10 req/s when not specified in config
HTTP 429 responses trigger automatic retry after Retry-After header delay (or 60s default)
Update scrape.test.ts to verify RateLimiter is created and passed to adapters
100% coverage maintained
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: This touches multiple files. The key change is threading the RateLimiter through scrape.ts → adapters. Existing adapter tests may need mock updates for the new parameter. Keep changes minimal in each adapter — just add acquire() calls before fetch calls.
